review: Product received for free. Everything is finally looking good! No crashes and running stably at 144fps on my 1070. This is still the original Skyrim + DLCs but it looks and feels much better. Highly recommend if you were a fan of the original version like me. PREVIOUS REVIEWSPlayed through the opening scene early today and experienced some serious issues. No full on crashes but I was experiencing some nasty FPS drops down to 7 8 from 110 for seemingly no reason. It happened specifically when the dragon comes down when you're about to get beheaded and while you're making your escape during character creation and in the catacombs. I was able to kind of hack my way around this by Shift+Tab opening the Steam Overlay briefly and that would bring the frames back up for a little bit.Skyrim is one of my favorite games ever and I will 100% play this but I'd wait to buy if you haven't until Bethesda can fix this and the other issues being reported.Update November 18 2016The framerate bug still exists bug crashes seem to have gone away for the most part. I've moved to the beta patches and would recommend those for everyone experiencing similar issues to me. Also I have found a workaround for the framerate drops. Go into your Nvidia Control Panel and under 3D Settings &gt Manage 3D Settings Program Settings &gt Sykrim Special Edition (full path of executable) Change "Monitor Technology" from "Use global settings" to "Fixed Refresh". You'll be capped at 60fps but it makes the game playable.Update November 24 2016Haven't been able to get a consistent 144fps for some reason but I think it may be due to the game not picking up the display adapter settings for whatever reason.

review: This game is described by the developers as a survival/crafting game and the graphics are absolutely gorgeous but it is so heavily biased towards murdering psychopaths I doubt it will ever be anything but a mass murder simulator. Largely because after two years in Early Access the developers have shown absolutely no interest in fixing the horribly broken gameplay which goes like this Every few weeks the entire map is reset because the servers can't cope with all the buildings and items hoarded by the first few players who joined. These very first few players who had the time to play non stop for 20 hours after the last wipe got to hoard some automatic weapons and build inpenetrable fortresses of steel and stone. After this they spend the next few weeks sniping naked would be players who try to join the game. See the established players spawn inside their fortress next to their chest full of armor weapons and medkits while everyone else spawn naked on a beach holding a rock which will fall apart if you try to hit a tree more than a few dozen times. Collecting wood will ofcourse get you nowhere because you need cloth (which is pretty rare) stone (which is nearly impossible to come by) and animal fat (easiest to obtain by killing yourself) to craft a simple furnace smelt 100 units of metal which can then be used to craft a combination lock which can be used to lock... well whatever you would have had to lock if you hadn't been killed a LONG time ago at this point. Because of this the game quickly devolves into a bunch of desperate frustrated naked guys pummeling eachother with rocks instead of "surviving" and "crafting". All of this is accompanied by the inspiring sound of microphone toting teenage misfits telling you to f**k yourself in poor english while dismembering your corpse with a rock. If you can play this game for a week without completely losing faith in humanity you simply haven't been paying attention.

review: I've 356 hours of my life away on FS 17 so naturally I bought this game 4 hours before release and....Its a more polished version of FS 17 with a few new features.And honestly thats great. I simply don't understand the people leaving negative reviews because the core gameplay is the same. What the hell did you expect? zombies? a battle royale mode? Theres only so much you can realisticly do in a game primarly about farming. Anyway...The bad Bugs. Ive encountered a few more since I first wrote a more positive version of this review about 4 hours in. The most glaring right now are a weird floaty physics issue after putting logs in a pickup and removing them a sound hiccup when using the chainsaw and a visual glitch with rain coming through the cab of certain vehicles. Ive also heard about multiplayer connectivity issues but as a single player only person I can't comment. These issues exist as of 11/20/18 Reported issues with connectivity and control bindings not sticking with wheels pedals ect. as of 11/20/18Seasons and the Follow Me mod still haven't been implimented into the base game. Seasons I can kind of understand since people have strong feelings on the mod both for and against so its absence is probably a calculated decision.Sim ers are a fickle bunchVehicle list is a bit small. That's been the case for every farm sim game on launch and has to do with licensing difficulties. Still if you're coming from a heavily modded version of fs17 you'll probably be a bit disapointed. The good While not mind blowing the graphics look a bit crisper and cleaner. In particular vehicle interiours look a lot less 'plastic y' Hard to descibe but compare fs17 and 19 and its noticable. The new start from scratch game mode is a lot of fun and so far works just as advertised.It's probably the only way I'll play the game from now on.The maps while small have alot more detail and are generally more fun to explore than those in base fs17. the devs clearly took insperation from the modding community. Sound improvements. the vehicle engine loops sound better and the rain sound effects are much better. Tweaked vehicle handling. Vehicles in FS17 all felt stiff and toylike. more like driving an RC car than a big piece of machinery. While still not perfect theres a sense of weight behind them now. There is however the physics issue mentioned above with pickups as of 11/20/18I haven't played long enough to mess around with horses the biggest new feature yet but overall Same game still good

review: EDIT RIght after typing my review a patch downloaded and I just tested it my Core2Quad issues have been resolved and it's playing with very good frames on that system with the 1050ti! GREAT job Devs. Just played this for 6+ hours straight. After trying to launch to play on my living room setup (and failing) I moved onto my desktop which is a much more powerful system. Living room Core2Quad Q9550 8gb DDR3 1050ti crashed right after launch (sometimes before). Tried all the fixes nothing worked. Hopefully they iron it out. EDIT They did and it's awesome but the controller/camera needs a bit of tweaking. Overall very happy!)Desktop i5 4670 24gb DDR3 R9 290 crashed only on the first launch. Never again after that in six hours of playing.Overall this is a very fun game even solo. I slowly figured out how to play as I went along eventually building a rover then skipping the truck and shuttle for a Spaceship. Launched and landed on several planets all very different looking but like NMS samey. There are no enemies to fight just a few plants that spew poison clouds (but can still kill you). There's grass to be mowed and collected for use in generators and there are many options to provide power and oxygen. You'll struggle at first but it's a fun struggle. I've had a lot of fun for 6 hours and the game is worth 20 dollars for sure. That said I played NMS for 60+ hours and I honestly really like that game for what it is and similarly enjoyed GRAV for many hours. This game feels like a cross between No Man's Sky GRAV and Scrap Mechanics and in some ways is better than all. NMS has more polish and feels like a more living universe maybe. And GRAV's combat is a bit more fun. But the environmental effects and hazards make this game a lot of fun. There will be tense moments. It definitely feels like an early access indie game. But in a good way.It seems the devs patched some things right off the bat (none of which helped my situation at first) and hopefully we'll see that continue in the coming days and months. (EDIT There was a patch waiting as I wrote this review that resolved my issues amazing job Devs.)I'm giving it a thumbs up but steer clear if you're running an AMD CPU for now. I hear there are some problems with those currently. However my AMD GPU had no issues running very nicely with my i5.Even though the game is simple looking graphically it seems to be proceedually generated (the two starting planets I tested were quite different) so the look of the game from trailers fool you into thinking the system demands won't be high. I expect there's a lot going on beneath the surface. No pun intended. I experienced a lot of frame loss especially on new planets and when my base got pretty large. I feel that on a game this simple looking (no/barely textures) it shoudln't be hard to run at max but again there's a lot going on and weather effects etc probably hamper that. Unreal Engine is notoriously a glutton for resources besides. (Re ARK.) Hopefully we'll see some better optimization soon. (Typically I was getting 40 80 FPS at 1440p though and the slow down wasn't enough to frustrate me much as it only happened rarely. It's very colorful the music is a great match for the feel and look of the game and the audio fx are suitably cool silly and spacey as well. I quite like it so far going to try to talk my gf into playing with me tomorrow now that the Core2Quad issues have been fixed.Good job devs. I'd love to see some creatures to fight and some silly/fun weapons perhaps a monitary system or something to save for in the long run. I found that the drill for the truck really doesn't do a hell of a lot compared to your own multitool and it fell off my truck a lot. At any rate I love it so far and can't wait to play multiplayer. I will certainy be putting many more hours into this little gem!

review: Short version of my review It was my wish that survival horror remained the same but if it had to change then this is the way to do it.9/10I feel like in the case of any remake the past experience of each individual with the original game plays a huge role in their opinion of the current iteration. RE is one of my favourite video game series and I have played all of the games extensively (yes even Gaiden). Like many others I consider the original RE2 the best of the bunch and while I enjoy RE4 and have played it more than 50 times on a variety of platforms I credit it with the downfall of RE and survival horror in general. I really liked RE7 for its return to horror themes and a more planned and tactical approach to combat but to me it never really matched the formula that makes a survival horror game which includes fixed camera angles and tank controls.Now comes the new RE2 and it took me by surprise when I saw it went TP over the shoulder. I was already disappointed I wanted a remake like the first and we were going to get a generic action game. How wrong I was.This game IS survival horror in the 21st Century. It is an amazing experience that brings back the tension of the old games and by that I mean the constant required planning of routes item carry and what to kill or ignore. I makes use of the well established setting and story and improves on it delivering more detail to the world and refining the gameplay to appeal to both newcomers and veterans alike. The new zombies are a less predictable and lickers are more deadly making your ability to aim a necessity rather than an overpowered mechanic. The new redesign of the RPD and the subsequent areas keeps things fresh but has many of the landmarks old fans will recognise especially in the beginning sections of the game. Some characters have their roles expanded like Chief Irons Marvin and Kendo but the story remains the same. Some enemies have been removed namely the spiders the crows and the moth while the G offspring was downgraded from boss to a powerful but numerous enemy. All the guns from the original make a return except for the Bow Gun but you won't really miss it. The gunplay is very satisfying and making your shots count is as important as ever just do yourself a favour and play on Hardcore. If there is something negative to say about this game is that the Devs probably rushed the A&amp B scenarios as they no longer complement each other making the experience rather repetitive. For instance aside from where you enter the RPD and the sequence of a couple of puzzles Leon A and Leon B are the same up until the end when you get an additional boss battle and the true ending cutscene. Leon no longer meets Claire in the RPD and they do not talk on the radio which I feel was a missed opportunity. I wanted to see more interactions between the main protagonists and a bit more character development but alas it does not really detract from the bulk of the experience. I wanted a traditional return to classic Survival Horror but instead got a modern masterpiece. This is Capcom's redemption and a rare time in which a Resident Evil fan can feel optimistic about the future. An absolute recommendation you owe it to yourself to play this game.

review: Wish I had gotten this game sooner. For those considering getting it. It's a very simple game. You play ball with cars and try to score goals while keeping your opponents from doing the same. The controls are very responsivel both on keyboard and mouse. And the game is just plain fun. I don't even typically like sports outside of watching it with a boyfriend usually and furthermore I don't much like to race cars either haha. So for me the fact that I ended up having so much fun here was quite interesting!The game features several games modes but I have only played 3 of them. The simplest ones in fact. 1v1 2v2 and 3v3. You can party up with friends from steam. The game features cross platform gameplay but I do not believe you can team up with friends on PSN I am unsure I don't have friends who play it on PSN. I never have to wait more than 30 40 seconds to enter a match no matter what mode I have tried. You can compete in competative gameplay in 2v2 and 3v3..and maybe even 1v1 but I'm not certain as I've never tried 1v1 competatively.The games soundtrack is among one of the best I have heard in a long time absolutely great soundtrack and sound quality. The DLC cars are pretty cheap cosmetics. But the game gives you a metric ton of cosmetics for free as you progress just for playing the game. As well as loot boxes which you could purchase keys for at I believe 1$ per key. Loot boxes offer random loot ranging from really useless to really awesome. Typical as far as that goes.You can trade loot boxes with people you meet in steam for keys and such so you essentially will never have to pay a dime if you don't want to. The community is fairly hit and miss as with any competative game just don't let the salty people get to you and you will be fine. The game does seem easy enough that anybody can get in and have fun but despite this it can get pretty hard to beat good players and it rewards learning how to do some pretty cool tricks using the rockets and angles of your car to hit the ball just right. All in all I really have no complaints about this game. Perhaps the only complaint is that it doesn't seem to punish the rage quitters but I am unsure since I am not one if that is true or not. You will see plenty of them in competative. Sometimes after the first few moments after the first score isn't your teams score. It usually snowballs from there into a total forfiet match. But when that does not happen the games go smooth and run fine and are really fun.Lastly getting back to the cosmetics..its really fun just messing around with your cars looks after unlocking new cool stuff to use. A fairly decent amount of customization is in the game based on what cosmetics you get ranging from paint jobs wheels antenna's rocket boost exhausts goal explosions toppers (cute little ornaments you can put on the top of your car like a witch or wizard hat for instance just to be silly) The sound of the engine..etc. For it's simplicity and plug and play ability I give the game a 10/10. I went into it expecting to hate it. But it exceeded my expectations by a huge margin and I really don't have any complaints about the game itself.

The game was unlike anything I had ever played before and even after my Xbox was sold off for some cash I bought it on PC and started from scratch. I spent far far too much time on this game and frankly... this 'update' wasn't needed. The original to be fair has dated a little but not enough to warrant a remake. I honestly would've expected Morrowind or Oblivion to recieve the make over treatment (which they both definitely need because my god they look like trash compared to Skyrim). This Special Edition also doesn't really add anything that mods in the original couldn't of done except the graphics hike isn't optional and if you're playing on a sub par computer like me isn't good. At least with the original I can pick and choose my graphical mods to customise my experience sure it might look a bit worse than the Special Edition... but I can run it.All in all I feel like this was just to milk the popularity of a modern classic from the 12 hours I've played nothing but graphical stuff and a few little immersive things have been added. Again this is all stuff you can get in the original with mods. They should've only released this for console I feel and added more graphical options for PC rather than a new game that can't have it's graphics lowered.However I appreciate Bethesda for quite literally just giving me the Special Edition I feel like that was a great move on their part. But Oblivion/Morrowind should've got this Special Edition not Skyrim. But if your PC can run this then enjoy it's still Skyrim.

review: I've played my fair share of Rust I got the game before the remake that is available now and it's safe to say I've played enough to know what I'm talking about.In it's core Rust is a beautiful and solid game with a good dev team who care about it and try to make it better every week with each update. The game mechanics are good if a little unbalanced and "wonky" at times.But this is where the real ugly comes in. Rust is as you know an early access game and it has been since it's release in almost 2 AND A HALF YEARS AGO! It has been 2 and a half years and the game is still stuck in ALPHA! Here you have a game that has been in an alpha stage of development while at the same time being accessible to the public for 2 and a half years that is absolutely unacceptable. This quickly ties in to my second problem with the game the perfect unbalance of player progression. Rust is survival game in which you start with nothing and need to build your way up so you'll be spending hours on end gathering resources to make your base and acquire weaponry. But the problem is that there are other players. And this makes for 2 thing 1 Rust solo is absolutely unplayble as you will definitely run into groups more often than not and lose everything you have resource gathering will take an obscene amount of time and there is no way you will manage to defend your base properly from again groups of players.2 Rust in it's current state is simply a deathmatch with a survival and crafting gimick implimented.I have tried several times to get back into Rust and enjoy myself but I just can't seem to be able to anymore.I definitely don't recommend you buy Rust in it's current state or ever for what it's worth.

review: EARLY ACCESS REVIEW Do you like COD ? Do you like counter strike ? Well maybe you should buy OVERWATCH if you haven't done that yet because this is not a fast paced FPS here you'll have to use your surrounding and your brain so forget about having high reflexes and such and let me explain you the pros and cons of this game.But first please note that FOR NOW if you are looking for a game that will let you gain level and the more you play the more you'll get skills point and such well then this is not in the game you play and every match is pretty unique you win/lose earn money buy a crate that contain a random cloth and you keep playing. There is a leaderboard and a ranked will come at some point.Pros A good variety of weapons You can customize aim sensibility and keyboard (and probably a controller) One match should last around 30 minute average if you are not a run and gun player Every match is different with some fixed elements that allow you to improve The map is huge and is pretty interesting Patching every weeks and one big monthly patch. A smart player can kill someone with fast reflexes Lots of tactics to use depending of the mode 3 mode Solo Duo Squad (4 players) 30$ for such a game is a good deal You can customize weapons by adding mods Not a pay2win (there is no ingame shop) Being cautious is rewardingCons 1 map (they are working on new maps) not fully optimized yet so having a bad PC won't help you Luck is a part of the game that is upon all of the players you may get lucky or not. It's a minor detail but it can bothersome especially players that talk about having "skills" they will get very annoyed. No kill cam server busy on week ends but who would knew that so many players would join the early access ? Not me. Some bugs and glitches but it's an early access so it's common.Overall If you are looking for something that is not an fast paced generic FPS and you want a game you could play all day or when you feel like it then this is probably a game for you.

review: Okay so I see that there are quite a few people who aren't happy with the game because of things like performance and bugs. I just want to adress these topics in a quick and helpful review based upon what I have experienced within the game. So yes the FPS does drop and stutter sometimes. I believe this to be due to lots of smoke grenades going off at the same time or just lots of stuff happening in general. However for me (I should note that I have a fairly good Mid High range PC) these FPS drops and stutters do not happen too often. There are also things like Graphics loading at the lowest setting when you respawn. To clarify most of the time when you respawn the graphics look really low res like lots of pixels and crap. However this problem fixes itself quite quickly and they return to the setting you have them on. I believe this is due to the engine they are using. The way I see it the game doesnt load the entire map in high res because that would reduce performance. So instead it loads the textures around you as you move around just enough that you dont notice. However it also does this when you are spectating someone so when you respawn all of a sudden you switch to a position where the game hasnt loaded the textures so they are low res. If you dont beleive me try switching players quickly when you are spectating. The same thing happens with the textures. I feel that the spectator camera hasnt been that well implemented into the game however hopefully this will be fixed later on.Next topic is the bugs. Things like guns and bodies getting stuck in walls and occasionally things like your hands and guns failing to load. I have experienced all of those bugs and to be honest are they annoying? Not really however the hands one does annoy me somewhat. But that can be fixed. I just want to note that is it a game? Yes. Have you ever played a game that had absolutely no bugs in it on release? I know I haven't. It's a game that just came out of early access. Expect bugs to be in it. Sure they delayed it 2 months but I feel that was for performance of the game. My point is bugs can usually be fixed quite easy nowadays so there's no point complaining unless it is a complete game breaking bug that should have been found and fixed by now.In conclusion is Sandstorm a good game? I think it is despite the obvious problems with the engine. The audio and visual effects of the game are absolutely stunning and I still somehow find an excuse to play the game for a little longer every time. There is no way to describe the feeling you get when you watch the A 10 strafe a target area. If you are a person who will not tolerate one or any of the things I mentioned above then you may want to hold off this game for now. If you are like me and you dont mind bugs unless they break the game then I would say make sure your computer can run it well and buy it.

review: Its a decent port however the game has a couple of quirks that really make it hard to recommend the game. The controls in game are okay however playing the game there are alot of small items that were not converted well for example one of them is the quick item use interface in game referred to as the radial menu which simply does not work with keyboard as it was designed for a 8 point axis e.g. a joystick. Even mimicking the general direction by pressing W A simply does not work and you have to use its clumsy scroll over one item at a time menu to access important items. This can really be annoying in a fast pace game like this when your trying to scroll between healing items capturing traps or etc. The chat interface takes 3 subcolumns in the menu to even access so you can't even simply press enter and type to your teammates which makes VOIP the only method of talking to your teammates in game as well.However even with all of this the one issue that I cannot write off on is its network issues. At the time of writing this review its almost nay impossible to actually connect and have a couple of hunts go well without the game disconnecting you or your teammates and this can be incredibly frustrating especially in a hunt where the difficulty settings do not dial down after a player leaves. The game will at sporadic times kick players off a hunt making the remaining players to fend for a boss thats meant for 4 people and often times you may find yourself kicked out of the session to face a boss thats now significantly harder then it should be. If your ultimately a solo player (which the game will adjust itself for) and you can deal with some quirks here and there then the game is fine for you. However if your looking for a dark souls esque experience where you can get help or join in on a boss once in a while then I recommend you to pass up on the game until the issues are resolved.

review: Online Is Fixed (For Me) EditionThe Good Combat feels very satisfying and weighty and offers a play style for everyone via the 14 different weapon classes that can be switched to freely between missions. Attacks can not be animation canceled so you have to be more calculated than in other action games which I feel is a nice change of pace. Overall the core gameplay loop of gathering materials hunting monsters and crafting/upgrading items and gear is quite fun. There's always something new to build toward or a new personal goal to meet. There's a lot of character in MHW from the weapon and armor designs that tell the story of what a given hunter has accomplished to the silly animations when diving or cooking just to name a couple of my favorites. You can even capture smaller creatures and keep them as pets in your personal quarters. Overall the game is very charming in so many different ways. Hell I can't stop humming that damn tune that plays at the HQ. Also can't wait for that free DLC.The Bad Online was broken for the first two weeks not acceptable. Game did not launch with any of the DLC that is already on console. Cutscenes are unskippable and doing co op in story missions is a pain since each person has to watch the cutscene in their own mission back out then make a new mission. The cherry on top is that the story itself is completely throwaway. It's not terrible but a story that evokes nothing is often times worse than something truly awful in its own way. No transmog armor despite overwhelming demand for it enjoy looking like a clown or having an unoptimized hunter. Performance on my i5 6600K + GTX 1070 was less than I expected. Lowest dip was to 30 when sleep bombing an Anji in the forest average is around 60 70fps with rolled back driver version 398.36.Verdict In most other games the bad things wrong with MHW would be so annoying despite being so small (like a gnat) I would never think to recommend it especially since I think most issues like the cutscenes transmog and story mission co op issues will never be fixed. So it's all that more meaningful for me to give MHW my overwhelming recommendation. The game is blast to play pure and simple and will only get better as the free updates roll out. This is my first Monster Hunter game and I've bought it three times. Once on PS4 once on PC for myself and again on PC for a friend. Despite its flaws I would not hesitate to do it again.

review: First and foremost this is an alpha. There will be bugs. The game is incomplete. Understand this before writing a review.All that said this game is great! I've never aspired to do anything more than collecting space dirt with an oversized suped up vaccuum cleaner then 3d printing stuff with that dirt. Astroneer teases you with tiny bits of visible resources at the surface of the planet leading you down a rabbit hole of needing to find out just how much is actually there. Once you've finished with that patch there's another one within eyeshot of the first. You want to go mine that one too but you've got to go back to base to refill on air and power. If only there was a way to carry more air or power so you could go out longer. Your first mission... You now have the means to stay out longer and you've cleaned out yet another pit of goodies and there's still more to find but your backpack is full... If only there was a way to carry more. Your second mission... This is what Astroneer is. It is the progression based space exploration and industry that drives everything that is fantastic about this game. It takes the resource gathering and machine building of Minecraft to make your job easier and pairs it with simplistic construction while still having a deep enough progression system that requires you to keep making trips out to build that next module.Playing this game even in its incomplete state has shown me what this game can be. With their suggested "automation" update and the dynamic ability to build sprawling planetary bases in whichever configuration desired is a recipe for hours of enjoyment in building the most efficient resource gathering pipelines anyone can think of. Couple this with interplanetary travel and you have the makings for Spore's resource trading on a smaller more intimate scale. And the best part is you will be the one who creates it all.This is probably one of the best "make your own fun" games I have played in a long time. There's not a lot here since it's an alpha but it's the potential that has me excited. It's what the developers have said they want to create that has me captivated. It's their communication and devotion to the project that has me in love with this game. I can't wait to see what it becomes...TLDR Buy this. Support the small team creating a game for gamers not the publishers. Be open minded and imaginative about what this game can and will become and you will have a fantastic time.

review: TLDRIf you don't (really) care about the online part of the game get it!If your primary reason to get this game is for its online part however please be aware that you'll have to grind money for many many hours in order to unlock the most fun things.SingleplayerIt's really a great singleplayer game! Yes it has its flaws and yes I would've liked to see some things done differently but it's still one of the most solid GTA games ever made in my opinion (don't cry San Andreas you'll always be my favorite baby). The thousands of mods available will make sure there's always something new to do in case you ever get bored of the vanilla game. Props to the developers on delivering this to us gamers!OnlineUnfortunately a lot less great. Don't get me wrong it can still be fun. In fact I used to enjoy playing online a lot. Heists and all that were great and just free roaming in the world was fun most of the time. For me this all turned around the moment the update with the big expensive ship was released. From there on I felt as if the most fun things were getting locked behind such a high price tag that you'd have to grind hours upon hours to get the money for it. This is not at all what GTA is about in my opinion. I do support having to earn money to buy things but as it stands today it's all way to much of a grind.Another unfortunate thing is that there are still a lot of "modders" to this day. On the one side you've got your fair player grinding away to unlock stuff. On the other you've got modders spawning everything they want in a matter of seconds and if they want can really annoy other players.A third thing is the shark cards you can buy with real money. Apart from the fact that I totally despise this business practice the prices are so outrageous that I'm just not going to waste any more time on this matter.So...I originally thumbed down the game because I felt the devs went the wrong direction with the online part which to me is a very big aspect of the game. However the game is still worth its money to those who mostly care about singleplayer. I figured it would be fair enough to thumb up for the good but with a mention of the bad.

review: I don't want to give the game a thumbs down because I really love playing both survivor and killer. They're both super fun and enjoyable however most of the reasons behind the game having any cons really comes back to the player.Pros Lots of variety. Each match is different from the last and no one strategy is gonna get you out alive or get each survivor. There are currently 7 killers and 7 survivors each with different perks that allow you to mix and match to customize how you play. Currently there are 7 (might be six?) maps to play on and each one requires you use different methods to hide from the killer or devise different tactics to outmanuever survivors. Both sides get to choose offerings and items to assist them which I absolutely love (and hate sometimes).Cons Cheaters. Loads of cheaters. People playing with their friend as the killer and taking the killer their friend to other survivors and then unhooking them so the killer can then hit and rehook them. Sometimes it can be hard to find a lobby as a survivor and when you do the killer's ping is so high you lag/rubberband and it's a terrible match for everyone. If you stick around someone on a hook too long as the killer you get fifteen invites to some kind of group mocking you for "camping". I also get called a myriad of names at the end of most matches but that's the internet more than a con.All in all I love the game but the people sort of put a damper on it. Don't be discouraged though if none of this sounds like too much of a downer and totally get it D

review: My experience with this game can be summed as thus every update I found myself testing the changes nodding in satisfaction then quitting the game to await the next update.Arkane knows how to make a good game. No question. But if you film an Oscar worthy movie and the lens is smudged while filming you can't judge what's underneath without acknowledging what's been marring your experience the entire time. PERFORMANCE Everyone is aware of the performance issues and these still persist to this day. It runs much better than at launch where it was literally unplayable but that's because the game looks worse than before the most noticeable change being the extremely aggressive LOD scaling. Out of the corner of your eye you notice the shapes of window frames and posters on distant buildings morphing in shape or the furniture at the opposite end of a long hallway suddenly blinking into existence. FPS dropped to 15 when stabbing a gravehound so they simply removed the inky visual effect that was causing the problem instead of optimizing it.Also Denuvo authentication is one of the longest "loading screens" of the game. Around half a minute to a full minute or more every startup. GAMEPLAY For the most part gameplay is excellent and is Dishonored's strongest suit. Dark Vision was changed to a blurry short range sonar so unlike Dishonored 1 you aren't constantly seeing blue and yellow because you had no reason not toAI is much smarterNonlethal combat options are a blastBonecharm crafting system allows for player flexibility and "builds"Each level feels lived in while maintaining the duality of directive flow and open options that made the first game so good.Emily and Corvo have distinct animations and final weapon upgrades. The animations are supremely cool.Each level is fairly distinct some with extremely interesting central "gimmicks." I do however wish the game relied less on them and had more "regular" areas.However under the hood lie other problems. Most of them are quality of life issues Gone are the hotkeys for journal inventory bonecharms powers. Only one "journal" exists now despite still having separate subsections.It took months for the power wheel to be fixed. It took almost a full second after activating to pop up and be usable breaking flow so badly I almost never used it in the first place. It's finally fixed now but this issue was glaring and it took so long to be addressed most of us played through without it fixed.Thrown objects don't always go exactly where your crosshair is. While this adds a layer of difficulty it feels noticeably more clunky than in the first game.Mana regen is pitifully slow. From using a power to fully regenerating Dishonored 1's time is 4.7 seconds &gt 3.1 seconds with Spiritual Pool. Dishonored 2's time with 4x Spiritual Pool is 6.3s &gt 5.5s. The devs said they fixed this effect but it was only made worse.Bugs. Street speakers not playing. Dying after possessing gravehounds. An arc pylon never shutting down after pulling out its power leaving it to either be dangerous to you to dangerous to your nonlethal playthrough. Some of these still aren't fixed. STORY AND ATMOSPHERE Reactivity Great. My favorite part of Dishonored. You need to hide from a gang member to access a certain black market shop and there are different scenarios and dialogue for if you hide if you run into him outside kill him outside or kill him inside.Emily and Corvo Emily and Corvo are voiced. And... they don't talk enough. It's good that they're silent for most of the game but there are times when you come across a portrait or photograph with an "Inspect" prompt. I'd love to hear Emily's thoughts on the High Overseer as see how that compares to Corvo's or if it changes based on whether or not you accept the Outsider's Mark. Instead all I get is the protagonist muttering the name of the person pictured. What's the point? Might as well keep them silent.It made sense to me to play Emily first but her story felt lackluster like people at every turn were saying "check your royal privilege" despite my efforts to resolve everyone's problems without drawing blood. Corvo's is MUCH more interesting as a veteran of Dishonored 1.The Outsider and The Void I hate the new Outsider and his new voice. He felt threatening and malicious in the first game due to how calm and composed he was and the Void felt like a strange and otherworldly place. The vignettes of Dunwall made it feel both unnatural and unnerving yet fundamentally woven into the universe. In Dishonored 2 it's just smoky blackness and sharp rocks. The Outsider is much jollier and moves around erratically making grandiose hand gestures. They actually had a plot plot that could explain this change but it was never addressed so it just seems like a pointless retcon to me.Main Plot Dishonored's worldbuilding was always one of its appeals and that remains true in Dishonored 2. However the villains felt lackluster. Only the main villain has a real presence throughout the game whereas everyone else feels introduced abruptly only to fall by your hand all within the same mission. In Dishonored 1 everything felt personal and real. Perhaps it was because of the long intro where you interacted with most of them or the Hound Pits's cast of characters all having different connections to your targets. As you can see I've played this game a LOT and have put a lot of thought into it. It was definitely worth all those hours and all that money but the condition it was at launch and the sluggish drip feed of support we barely get now is unacceptable. To set a precedent for future games I can't recommend buying this unless they manage to fix all the performance issues and bugs which doesn't seem to be happening anytime soon.

Now although there are people who can ruin the experience by disconnecting (honestly I take it as a compliment knowing they won't win so they quit . ) Don't let it deter you from playing an excellent game. review: As a disclaimer I came to this game a little late (June of 2017) and therefore did not have to contend with all of the early major bugs. I also adore horror so I am totally biased in that department HOWEVER this game has sucked me in. I'm addicted. I'm primarily a solo RPG gamer so this was a huge shift from my comfort zone. Here's what impressed me *The maps are procedually generated to a certain degree so that every game feels slightly foreign. *The tension of the game is fantastic from both the Killer and Survivor perspectives and keeps the horror element alive throughout each match.*It doesn't shy away from the gore.*Great game to play with random people but it really shines if you play "Survive with Friends" mode as it adds an extra layer of comaraderie.*When playing as the killer if another player is greifing you you just murder them. It's fun you should try it. What annoyed me *While the bugs do not break the game it does make certian matches grueling when pallets and such don't respond as they should. *The matchmaking system is a little flawed. Don't be surprised if you end up facing an OP expereinced opponent while you're still new. *Finally you have to patient in the lobby sometimes while waiting on a game. I keep my sociology textbook at my desk so I can study while waiting. Seriously read a book knit a scarf learn another language in the downtime. You'll be impressed by what you accomplish. I would recommend this game 100%. The free DLC that are released on a semi regular basis is nice and the paid DLC are not that over priced either.

As you drive past cow pastures corn fields and strange European cities you will contemplate your life your existence and what drove you to even purchase the game in its first place. When you're hauling manuer from Paris to Cologne you are actually driving deep inside your soul to truly discover yourself. I have personally witnessed people breaking down into tears as they latch their trailer and carry their load off into the sunset.I have few criticisms of this game with one exception The only proper setting is clearly America. After driving for over 50 hours I have yet to spot a single Bald Eagle. This clear lack of freedom is unexceptable and I expect this to be fixed in future DLC. And whether you're killed by wolves bears or naked jumping men with shotguns you will keep going because you want to be at the level of your killers. All of your work days of gameplay can be wiped out within 10 minutes. Oh yeah did I forget to mention that when you close Rust you don't disappear from the game world? Instead you lie on the ground sleeping. Anyone can walk up kill you and take all of your inventory. Fun right? Now I know it probably seems from this like Rust is a mean terrible death trap. review: Let me start by saying I LOVE this game. I love the cometitive cat and mouse style "horror" (thriller) feel it has. I like that it requires a different kind of skill set than other competitive based games like CS GO. I most of all love the devs for having an amazing amount of inspiration for this game.Sadly This is a prime example of what happens when an ambitious developer team releases a product too early.This game shows great promise but in all honesty it feels like an early access game that simply was pushed out of beta to increase sales give the illusion of significant progress etc.The game has significant balancing issues and countless bugs (god forbid you get stuck in hell hill's cracks) and now that this game has picked up a significant player base the devs are feeling the pressure and are struggling to fix the numerous bugs that should've been squashed in beta.One of the game's most unique aspects seems to also be its biggest problem Extremely competitive matchmaking.Due to the (forced) ranking system and no truly "casual" matches being available unless you create a private match with friends the playerbase should expect the ranking system (or even the LOBBIES) to be polished and developed.They are ANYTHING BUT THAT.You not only spend a significant time trying to even enter a lobby (especially if you have friends or a non 20 rank) but you also have to deal with getting matched with COMPLETELY RANDOM RANKS disgusting P2P and rampant point farming. This feels lazy of the developers to so blatantly ignore and these problems should've been fixed a long time ago.Honestly I know that this game wasn't expected to become so popular so fast and that the devs were surely overwhelmed due to this but if they had prioritized these massive bugs and balances from the beginning this game would have been a far better experience. (as of currently)But i'm also very glad that this game exists in this interesting competitive style and I know this should will become something great in the (not so far) future. As of currently i'd give this game a 7.5/10. Thanks Behavior Interactive!

review: Ok as I played the console version of the game for around 600 hours I feel as if I can give this port a decent review (Yes I said port.)Honetly the core game here is great just as it was on console the port is where you run into most of the negatives. Now don't get me wrong I love this game and wanted this launch to be smooth sailing but it just isnt anywhere near smooth. I will list the problems myself and others have ran into thus far with the game.1. Constant disconnects from the in game servers basically break this game when you get DC'd in this game the monster will stay scaled as in it's health will scaled up based on the amount of people that were in your game before disconnection. In turn this makes it to where you have to solo a monster that has 4x the health it would normally have along with 4x the resisitance to it's parts being broken. In my opinion this is game breaking and will literally make it to where you have to play the game solo until this is fixed. 2. The steam overlay...boy oh boy do I love being told about 20 to 30 times per session that I have a friend playing MHW and it tends to do this to the same buddy of mine over and over and over. I finally had to go into my Library&gt Right click MHW&gt Go down to properties&gt Check the box to disable the use of the steam overlay in game. That has been the only way to solve this issue currently until they deploy a hotfix etc. 3. The game has some very very bad FPS drops in certain parts of this game the Kushala fight for instance is abysmal my frames drop down in the teens at the ned of that fight due to it spawning 3 to 5 wind funnels. This game is nothing more than a port to the PC the textures look worse on here than they did on both my Xbox One S and my X granted of coruse my X is 4k and plugged into a 4k TV. The fact that people are having issues running this game on max with any of the 10 series cards is amazing to me this game really doesn't look that great and isn't really that dmemanding besides a few of the fights that are high in use of partical effeects etc. Why this took half a year I have no idea.4. Controller support is very spotty I know it says only partial controller support is currently supported but seriously why after this long would this game not have full controller support. MY xbox controller is connected wirelessly via BT and randomly in game my charachter will get locked into spinning motions hammer charges etc. It happens very periodically and is so spotty I have not found a way to resolve this as of yet. At the end of the day yes there are multiple negatives with this game but as I stated above the core gameplay is still very much intact and is great and highly addicting which is why this game peaks around 250 000 players a day but with these current issues I honestly can't reccomend this to anyone until these issues are resolved. Final Rating 7.5/10

review: For all those doubting how good early access games can be I am here to put your mind at rest. Unlike DayZ or H1Z1 which recieve updates maybe bi monthly( if you're lucky) which gives Steam Early Access a bad name Rust devs update the game weekly with a major overhaul coming on 7/7. The game runs very smoothly and throughout my 30+ hours of gameplay I never expierenced any crashes or game breaking bugs. Overall it is much like Kerbal Space Program ( the only other early access game i have invested money into) in the fact the game could be classified as a complete game but the devs want to maximize the game before they release into beta or beyond. As for gameplay.... my initial thoughts were that the game would basically be a "good graphic" minecraft but that couldn't be further from the truth. Instead the game has very realistic survival elements and hefty bullet drop/sprays which to some might be a negative. To me however these realistic elements give the game shape and form allowing the player to feel more enticed to play and get better with practice. I feel it is very important to distingush playing solo and with friends... When playing solo you will die and you will die ALOT but that comes with the territory. Although they can be boring after countless hours I highly recommend playing on lower pop servers in order to help make the game more enjoyable as you learn the basic mechanics. However even on these low pop servers the game is still highly enjoyable and you don't have to worry as much about Clans one of my biggest cons that I will get to later. As for playing with friends the game is A BLAST and there is no telling how much fun stuff can happen as you all work together to make a badass base and go looting for better equipment.The biggest pro imo is raiding. Raiding allows those who have invested quite alot of time and resources on a server to go and raid other players bases. There are two types of raids in the game Online raids and offline raids. Online raids are rarer and much more difficult to accomplish because online raiding literally means raiding someone's base why they are online but are much more rewarding and enjoyable if successful. Offline raids are the type 95% of players will expierence and occurs when someone raids your base while you are offline. These offline raids are the reason it is so imperative you make as strong of a base as possible before you log out and why playing with friends is much more enjoyable and encouraged.The biggest con goes hand in hand with raiding and is Clans. Clans are basically a group of people who form a huge base somewhere on the map and in order to protect their base and ensure server dominance basically give their members "jobs" in which it's X members duty to log in from 7am noon and watch the southeast side of the base for possible raiders or farm resources. hunt etc. These clans can be quite an annoyance and of the 4 servers I have played on 3 were ruthless doing anything and everything they could to insure dominance. If this sounds like something you cant handle I wouldn't recommend buying the game because nearly every server has a clan already in place.Overall the game is a refreshing survival game providing thrilling expierences as you go scavenging for resources raiding or just through exploring the map as you try your best to try and gain prominance in the server. For anyone interested in fps survival pvp or exploration I highly recommend this game as it masterfully combines all these games into a PC must own.Final Verdict 8/10 a great game well worth the $20 price tag and even more so if you can get it cheaper. However with the upcoming xp system about to be introduced and everything else the devs have in store I am certain this game can easily bump up to a 9 or a 10 and will update this post with more incite as the game evolves!

review: Rewriting my review since I actually enjoy playing the game and the game is finally below 50% score.I'm still LR (low rank) and have 30 hours at the moment while writing this also this is my first Monster Hunter game. The game is very fun and I had a blast playing with others. The design to the game and its mechanics are good. This is a perfect adventure game with multiplayer if everything goes alright. There's an expansive item and crafting system so there's a lot of utility and builds. Player classes are based off weapons you are carrying. Every monster is unique has strengths and weaknesses and monsters have states in combat. There's very good game design.However there are many issues in this game/port. I don't have as much as a problem with FPS etc because I have an Intel i7 7700k and an AMD RX 580 so I get 50 60 FPS. Older hardware will have MANY ISSUES! Especially how DENUVO (DRM) requires that your CPU has the FMA3 instruction set otherwise the game will crash. The multiplayer design is really bad where posted quests only show up in your 16 maxplayer sessions otherwise you need to use SOS flares in the field/quest to reach ALL sessions where rewards are disabled for joiners when 10 min in the quest passes. You are unable to coop story missions from the start because it's solo restricted at the start of all story missions where you have to play to a certain part and watch cut scenes first. So don't expect to play through the whole game with your friends as you will have to fight against the game's multiplayer system to do that it's truly atrocious. But it's ok if you play with randoms only. This game also has DENUVO where you have to be online to play and it's a pretty heavy duty DRM so watch out. And lastly as of now there are network/server hiccups/errors that sometimes randomly happen where you will be disconnected from your sessions even if you create the session and it's only you. You are required to be in a session to do any sort of multiplayer.If you can deal with all the cons then the game will be very fun and worth the buy in my opinion

review: Everyone talks about how it's early access bugs blah blah blah. If you're reading this review you know about all that. I recently realized I am a huge fan of survival sandbox games and I have played quite a few in the last months. Here is my personal impression of this one.Graphics are incredible. I know everyone has said this but it needs repeating. On the lowest settings it still looks awesome! Some clipping and such but it never really bothered me much.It's very fluid (no pun intended) to get into it. I agree with most other reviews that recommend no using guides and such and just jump into the deep water (pun intended) and learn to swim on your own. It's a very friendly interface that gives just enough explanation to make you feel like you can do it on your own but not enough to make it boring.Edit I forgot the most important part (to me at least.) The metabolism for food in this game is very nice. In plenty of other games like this you have to eat every two minutes or face death from starvation. In this game keeping hydrated is the issue. While this is rather ironic while being surrounded by water it makes a lot more sense. I get away with eating once every day or two depending on my activity. Dehydration keeps me drinking daily but not constantly. Considering dehydration kills you faster than starvation I feel this is the most realistic representation I have seen in one of these games thus far. Here is what any new player needs to know Expect it will hurt you until you prove to yourself that it can't. Explore. Even the dark and scary areas. They usually have the best loot.Storage cubes cannot be used indoors (as of the writing of this review.)Predators are everywhere and you are not one of them. If it can eat you it will.If it can eat you it's usually in a scary area.You WILL get snuck up on and jumpscared. Give it at least an hour before you start looking up stuff online and once you do do it very sparingly. Discovery is an awesome feature to this game and the more you have to figure out the more valuable this game will be.

Survivors and killers alike both have the mindset no matter what that the other is directly going against them not only in game but in overall moral code and feelings shared with eachother. I have almost never seen anyone on the survivor side agree with the killer and vice versa. One key example that I have seen the community do to reflect this is mass reviewing the game if a side got mechanics changed against their favor only giving negative reviews because of a simple change. Ranks 20 16Ranks 20 16 consists of people who are new to the game. Conversation is usually pretty open consisting of sharing ideas to general talk. Essentially the community that you would want to see from a developers standpointRanks 15 6Ranks 15 6 generally have your standard gg's and maybe some back and forth communcation here and there although there is some people who stand out from the bunch here and there.Ranks 5 1Ranks 5 1 are where the true community shows out. There is usally little talk if any at all and most of the time only a few gg's if you play right in the opposing player(s) eyes. Developers The developers for this game are a mixed bunch. They have made some awkward decisions ranging from balancing to just gameplay mechanics. The best example would be in patch 2.2.0 with pallets having only stun if the killer is essentially inside of the pallet. There isn't too much to hate on here besides that you can tell the developers are scared to make changes because their community hates change. The GameGameplayThe base gameplay is balanced in favor of the lower ranks (Rank 20 16). This has made playing in higher ranks feel too hard for every killer except what is generally considered high tier killers with nurse being the best as of now. The gameplay after 1k hours feels repetitive and I find myself coming back during high ranks only for the new chapters which to be fair usually come with their own rank resets. I feel as the gameplay would be more fun if there was either something to boost the baseline killer to have a higher skill ceiling or to make gameplay slower and less competitive the higher the rank you are.BugsBugs have plagued this game since its start being nothing but even more stress on the player. The PC side of the game has PTB's or Public Test Builds every once in a while. Each build usually contains a few bugs and what feels like every PTB the developers let through a few bugs or bad changes and release the chapter even though they exist. This on top of the community have made me question if I should have spent time playing the game to begin with. Conclusion Overall I feel as if the game is incomplete. It deffinetly needs a massive change to feel fun again in my opinion whether by making a casual mode or by making bonuses for being in high ranks. There honestly isn't much to say about it other than it is what it is a simple 4v1 game that gets harder to play the more you play it.I'm giving this game a no simply because of the dedication and patience you have to put into it to keep your sanity and to keep your anger down while playing it.All edits so far have been for formatting.

review: 8/10 for the graphical updates. It looks a lot better than vanilla skyrim (despite claims to the contrary). The vastly improved shadows are the real improvement here. At noon on a sunny day is where it's most apparent it's not the flickery shadowed mess it used to be. Other times of day have big improvements too and sunsets are beautiful (if a bit overblown).The Volumetric Lighting/Godrays are overdone in foggy weather especially in the rift but also stunning at times the throat of the world or markarth looming over you and casting a huge shadow is impressive. As for DoF I turned depth of field down (but not off) because my character isnt myopic.Also.... Precipitation occlusion has been added! This is the biggest thing for me in regards to the updates real shelter they didnt capitalise on that and add more violent weather however which brings me onto....3/10 for effort.I know bethesda never said this would be anything more than a graphical update. But I really think it was a missed opportunity to really reboot this game and fix blatent issues and gameplay problems. Bugs? Gaps in magic gameplay? (backpedal and die) Light vs Heavy armour gameplay? Archery? Many people have learnt from 5 years of modding and improvements and the games failings really came to light over the years (I would have happily payed for a reboot like that).Finally. The game runs super smooth feels great and loads quickly. Even with the open cities mod my game runs at a fairly stable 60 fps on my old GTX760 high settings... the modding potential for this improvement to performance cant be understated.PS Hurry up with the public CK release please.

review: Do not listen to the negative reviews of this game. Dead by Daylight has been an awesome experience that I'm still enjoying and will continue enjoying for months to come. First off here is what bothers me (and almost everyone else too) The connection when getting chased by the killer will almost garuntee that if you hop through a wall and the killer swings at you youre probably going to take a hit even though you're well past the wall. This is aparently because the game is hosted by the killer when you're in the lobby. So you as the survivor you need to take that knowledge onto the field and attempt to escape another way if you think that youre going to get screwed going through a window. WITH THAT BEING SAID. I love this game. Almost every game I enter my heart starts beating and the adrenaline rush hits me. You probably wont be good at this game for a day or two until you grasp some of the main functions of escaping the killers grasp. Like hiding breaking the running marks enough to confuse the killer using your perks the correct way and applying team work when you cannot communicate with the other survivors.The maps have some of the same looks but theyre all each procedurally generated so nothing is usually exactly the same. This witholds both the killer and the survivors the "home field advantage." However if you play the game enough youll begin to learn how to out manouver the killer so that youll have just enough time to make a quick getaway. Each killer has their own special ability so you'll get to learn how they each function and how to best beat them. The same thing goes for the survivors. Everyone has their own thing that will help out their teamates and make it about teamwork. All in all I'd give this game an 8 out of 10. Try it out with a friend. It's a lot better than playing solo.

review: After 41 hours I feel like I'm ready to say my piece about this game. It's important to specify that I'm playing in survival mode where you have to constantly worry about food and water. The game will be very different depending on which mode you play because in the sandbox mode you can freely build and explore without ever having to stop what you're doing to gather nourishment. In hardcore you have to be extra careful because once you die you have to start over. At this point I'm glad I did not pick hardcore because there are ways you can die that just aren't forseeable. There also occasional bug in the game which results in your death like the all too common diving reel malfunctions.First Impressions This game is amazing. That can be and is said about many games. But there is nothing like Subnautica. I had been waiting for 19 years ever since playing the crap out of the incredibly immersive fun but ultimately flawed Sub Culture. Finally we have a game that surpasses Sub Culture in every aspect except the storyline. With that said Subnautica has flaws.The Bad In all it's glory there are a few nags some of which make the game increasingly difficult as you get further into the game. First I'm going to get it out of the way that there is a startup bug that made me almost request a refund even before getting into the game. Subnautica doesn't always start because the game menu screen frequently refuses to fully load. This is probably some sort of GPU initialization issue that prevents the graphics from displaying properly. In any event I have to exit out of the game and restart it in Window mode to get the game to finish loading at all.Also The learning curve is very steep. There are no instructions for anything and the information given on any device in the crafting menus tell you nothing worthwhile about what stuff does. There are some basic descriptions but they're very poor. For example the current generator says it generates current. When I started playing I had no idea what I would want to create a current for.The third thing is the max depth of the in game vehicles. There is much debate about the actual depth of the game. Some say it goes on forever. Others have quoted that the game crashes out at 60 000 meters. Some have said 20 000 meters. Others have said there is a secret world in the greatest depths which sounds pretty epic. In any event. The ocean goes deeper than I feel comfortable thinking about. The problem here lies in the fact that the vehicles seem to have a max depth of 200 meters. (I've since found the Cyclops can go to approximately 900 meters at the expense of power efficiency. I believe the Seamoth can also go to a comparable depth.)Fourth the hunger and thirst meters drop far too quickly. This seems nitpicky when you consider I did pick the survival mode but the problem with this system is that you have to spend hunger and thirst to find food that becomes increasily more difficult to find as the game goes on. As a result you might find yourself spending almost half your time gathering food and supplies to make water. Which leads me to the next problem in the game.Fifth scarcity of food and supplies for making water. At first everything is plentiful and readily available. Salt while a challenge to find when you don't know what you're looking for seems to respawn readily and limitlessly. Coral while seemingly limitless at first begins to disappear rapidly after many hours of gameplay. Moreover I have seen no indication that it respawns. Food which pretty much comes from the natural fish stocks can disappear amazingly fast from an area. After 41 hours of gaming I have effectively cleared all of the initial shallows of the ocean plus the surrounding depths of fish. It's amazing how fast they diminish. The only solution seems to be to put respawning or faster reproduction of the fish in the game. I have not seen any indication that the fish respawn at all which seems clear by some of the dead zones I have in my current save. There are some pretty heated debates about this in the discussion groups. Naysayers claim the supplies are unlimited and all you have to do is look further. My answer to that is that you begin to spend a lot more thirst and food meter energy and other resources to find food. Because of this there is a rapidly diminishing return on the value of food and water in the game. The devs claim it causes people to explore more. I'm not satisfied with that response because the reality is this if people have no motivation to explore. If they just stick to the shallows and eat and drink they aren't going to have the attention span to stick with the game for the long term anyway. Apparently a fix is being tested in the experimental mode but it's coming all too slow to a stable build.Sixth and my final gripe and this is definitely as glaring as the fifth scarcity of resources. Copper Quartz Acid Mushrooms are plentiful at first but become ridiculously difficult to come by as the game goes on. Quartz is practically used in everything because you need it for glass and rubber which you need for building and making Power Cells to power your vehicles. Each Power Cell takes a vast amount of resources which would not be as much of a problem if they didn't deplete so rapidly. Even with the power efficiency mod only a small expedition can use 6 power cells and leave you scrambling for resources. Many users have defaulted to the same argument they have given to the food shortage problem that there's plenty in the depths. The problem is that it takes more and more energy food and water to farm this stuff. You end up trapped in a cycle of more and more rapidly diminishing marginal utility on all of your resources. This really needs to be fixed or users will basically be driven out of their own game by scarcity. Both of the last two problems have people vehemently defending the current scarcity with the argument that resources are scarce in real life. I would like to point out however that one person alone in a wilderness does not leave vast expanses of land void of any life. Certainly these rich biomes should be able to support just one person. Also if the player were able to hunt for shellfish and crustaceans in the game diversity of foods might help lower depletion rates. The player should be able to find oysters and dig for clams. The Good Based on my criticisms some might get the idea that I don't like the game. That couldn't be more wrong. Subnautica is hands down simply the best underwater game ever made. There's no competition. The environment is rich full of wonder and among the most immersive games I've ever played. The world is packed full of fascinating creatures beautiful vegetation and unparalleled undersea effects. The graphics are complimented by some of the most incredible sound you could possibly imagine. All of it adds up to a game that makes you feel like you're living rather than playing.It's one of those games that comes along and really changes things forever at least among those who have played it. In my opinion the game hasn't gotten nearly the recognition it deserves. The amount of stuff you can do in this game and the painstaking attention to detail are mindblowing. Those are things I hope never change with Subnautica. Many early access games are dumbed down in later iterations. Unknown Worlds Entertainment seems to have a good attitude about adding new features instead of taking them out like some other developers of early access releases have done in the past. I just hope they maintain the trend.Subnautica is an oustanding game worth its price about three times over. It comes with my highest recommendation. In it's current state I would give Subnautica a 9/10.Added 11/23/17 The game has been hugely updated since this review.

review: Alright let me make this as short as i can do you like games? i mean do you? yes? no? well if the answer is yes this is a Game yes an actual video game no "life service" no "platform" no "always online multiplayer because we can't make money with single player games anymore" t it's the real deal a GAME. First and foremost let me say this It's an absolute masterclass in Survival Horror well considering the early RE titles are themselfes the ones that started this genre proper it shouldn't be a surprise. Now since this is a complete remake the story was slightly altered and modernized in a good way the progression is slightly different than the original but most notably we get the RE4 6 Third person action camera that really stands out this time around because RE2 is the PERFECT fit for this over the shoulder camera angle which manages to really give the game a claustrophobic feeling and adds a lot of "gravity" to the overall gameplay. Guns feel heavy gunshots feel impactful and overall the gameplay itself is just excellent if you like well action games.Now let's get to the one thing that will probably turn off people who never played any game before 2010 The controls CAN be clunky but it is part of the design boss fights in particular can make you curse a lot because both leon and claire somewhat behave like trucks on a muddy road during those but this is a deliberate part of the design so you commit to your action and strategie going forward bolstered by it's particular focus on resource management and the overall theme of planning ahead for a few minutes. Now a lot of people that are not used to these kinds of concepts will curse the game while i sat there and admired how well all of the gameplay functions synergize and how well executed the entire thing is. Another "con" could be said about the game's lenght my first playthrough took me about 6 hours (while clearing out the entire game all items every room accessible with that character etc) and the second scenario took me a tad longer cause i chose to play leon first and claire second (claire being the harder of the two due to slightly less powerful weapons and i believe she also takes a bit more damage overall). So overall i'd say the average player will probably spend 7 9 hours per playthrough which amounts to about 17 20 hours for the "full story". But there is a TON more to do afterwards re explore the different scenarios try to optimize your time for higher rankings and unlock new guns and outfits etc. And yes you actually have to PLAY to unlock guns/skins/outfits for your characters you can't spend 20 bucks on it.. you actually have to play.. unbelievable the nerves on this dev eh? And the most unbelievable part of this all? FREE DLC coming feb. 15 with 3 new scenarios that's what i call madness! MADNESS!Well turns out this was rather long so sorry for this yet i haven't even touched on some of the most important aspects of the game so to wrap it up here are a few more bullet points that might be of interest Great optimization (running over 250+ fps maxed out (1440p) on a Vega 64 a SINGLE Vega 64 yes my rig has 2 but that'd be a waste of electricity at that performance) 4K runs at around 120 140 with like i said everything maxed out except deactivated Motion Blur and Depth of field for personal preference. Sometimes cheesy sometimes good story backed by STRONG performances from the voice actors (well done!) Still since the original some of the best level design in gaming history backtracking that doesn't feel like work but an actual revisit with a few twists here and there. Despite what i said about the overall controls earlier the Keybinds for PC are PERFECT you can certainly see this isn't a simple console port but done by people who know and understand PC players. NO SPIDERS! (yay!) Thanks Capcom from the bottom of my heart thank you for this cause i would have otherwise missed out on this amazing experience! Keep them out of the RE3 Remake too please! )

review: A boss fighting game like any other were you punch a brick for hours and if you ever miss a dodge you die. How this game is unique is you have a set amount of time to kill the boss preventing you from playing smart and waiting for opportunities and forcing you to constantly run towards and enemy that more than likely has an attack up its sleeve that can kill you in one hit. 90% of the time the boss can fly so it uses this ability to waste your time the only way to counter flying is with a limited amount (3) consumables that force it to land for 2 seconds each. Like other boss fighting games you will find that the monsters only take damage to one area but unlike other boss games I have played you use Japanese anime weapons that are ridiculously large so you will swing for the neck hit the wing with a downward strike reflect off and be stunned for a few seconds. After doing damage to the boss it will run away from you to the opposite corner of the map forcing you to chase it and waste more time. That is the game rinse and repeat there is a story in the back ground but all the characters have a distinct Japanese feel to me that means over the top and insanely annoying. The entire premise of the game is you are part of a group of monster hunters when you are at base there are people around but they never help you in fights. Even if the story tells you that this dragon is like a god and you are going to need all the help and luck you can get. When you get back to base they don t even treat you like you are the only one doing anything they act like they all contribute to the cause. This isn t really unique to monster hunter but I think it bothers me more in this game because these people have been on the continent for like 40 years or something and no one accomplished anything till you showed up. In the end the game feels supper mediocre to me but the games has sold enough copies that I m sure they will make more pc monster hunter games in the future the only question is if they will be willing to change the formula much. In the end I bought this game to play with a friend and after you leave normal skill quests in this game you kinda are forced to play the game with others because otherwise the game just isn t fun.
